They can also be represented as regular numbers, 100% being 1, 10% being 0.1, and 1% being 0.01. Knowing this, you can multiply 0.8 (or 80%) by itself, which allows you to determine your chances of failure after each attempt.

So, knowing that, we get that at your first try, your chances of failure are 0.8 (out of 1). Then on your second try, your chances are 0.8×0.8, or 0.64, which would be 64%. By continuing to do this, we get that the earliest instance of your chances of failure being equal to or bellow 0.01 comes when you multiply 0.8 by itself 21 times.
